problem: The population $P(t)$ of fish in a pond after $t$ weeks can be modeled by the differential equation ${P}^{′}(t)=0.09P(t).$ If the fish population was $8\,000$ after $18$ weeks, calculate the fish population after $23$ weeks.
worked_solution:
The general solution to the given differential equation is

$$
P(t)={P}_{0}\,{e}^{0.09t},
$$

where ${P}_{0}$ is the initial fish population.

We are given that after $18$ weeks, the population was $8\,000.$ So, substituting $t=18$ and $P(18)=8\,000$ into our general solution and solving for ${P}_{0},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(18) & ={P}_{0}\,{e}^{0.09\cdot 18} \\ 8\,000 & ={P}_{0}\,{e}^{1.62} \\ {P}_{0} & =\frac{8\,000}{{e}^{1.62}} \\  & ≈1\,583.190,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Hence, our particular solution is

$$
P(t)=1\,583.190\,{e}^{0.09t}.
$$

We want to find the fish population after $23$ weeks. So, substituting $t=23$ into our particular solution, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(23) & =1\,583.190\,{e}^{0.09\cdot 23} \\  & =1\,583.190\,{e}^{2.07} \\  & ≈12\,547,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest whole number. 

Therefore, approximately $12\,547$ fish will be in the pond after $23$ weeks.
